messages:
maria (runtime): Ran a targeted perf sweep on the A100 staging pool. Observed ~15-22% tail latency regression for causal SDPA when head_dim=30 and seqlen>=1024.

arjun (ml-opt): ugh, head_dim=30 again. that's not 32-aligned so tiling/warp packing differs. did autotuner pick a different kernel?

maria (runtime): autotune log shows it picked FlashAttention v2 non-causal kernel for many combos where we expected v3 causal path. snippet: 
```
[autotune] arch=A100 seqlen=1024 head_dim=30 batch=4 -> picked=flash_v2_noncausal (est=2.1ms)
[autotune] arch=A100 seqlen=1024 head_dim=32 batch=4 -> picked=flash_v3_causal (est=1.6ms)
[autotune] arch=H100 seqlen=512 head_dim=30 batch=8 -> picked=flash_v3_causal (est=0.9ms)
```

arjun (ml-opt): interesting — on A100 v2 non-causal seems to be chosen even for causal requests due to relaxed kernel compatibility checks?

zach (eng): I saw a fallback path in the runtime: if head_dim % 16 != 0 we avoid the tight v3 kernel and fall back to v2. That was intentional for correctness, but perf hit varies by arch.

jen (sre): is this reproducing on Dedicated (reserved) too, or only hosted A100 pool? customers might notice.

maria (runtime): reproduced on both hosted A100 and our dedicated staging cluster with same driver stack. H100 doesn't show regression — autotuner picks v3 causal there.

maria (runtime): quick repro snippet I used: 
```bash
python -m scripts.perf_runner --model gpt-small --backend sdpa --head-dim 30 --seqlen 2048 --batch 2 --device a100-staging
```

perf-ci-bot: Perf check: baseline=1.8ms median, current=2.1ms median, tail(95)=+18%. Regression flagged on channel eng-runtime.

arjun (ml-opt): two angles: 1) autotuner scoring model doesn't include causal vs non-causal execution cost delta per arch (we assume symmetric), 2) tiling heuristics for head_dim not robust for non-32 multiples.

zach (eng): Also KV cache behavior interacts here: for long context we use prefix-KV and the effective seqlen distribution skews, so batching heuristics pick smaller batches which amplifies per-request kernel overhead.

maria (runtime): I captured cudaProfiler output. there's an extra kernel launch and a memcpy around the SDPA call for head_dim=30 on A100. on H100 that memcpy is absent.

arjun (ml-opt): That memcpy suggests we hit a slowpath that remaps layout. Could be our alignment pad for shared memory. Need to check tiling code path: tile_warp vs tile_lane selection.

maria (runtime): attaching a short log excerpt: 
```
[profile] sdpa_call: kernel=sdpa_flash_v2_noncausal grid=(128,1,1) block=(256,1,1) time=1.82ms
[profile] layout_copy: malloc->device memcpy size=12288 time=0.38ms
[profile] total token cost ~2.20ms
```

jen (sre): customers using Dedicated with head_dim odd values might be impacted if they push long seqlen prompts. We should triage before next deploy.

arjun (ml-opt): proposed fixes: (A) update autotuner model to include causal/non-causal mode as a feature and per-arch calibration, (B) add a small compatibility shim: when head_dim % 8 == 0 but not %32, try v3 kernel with safe padding to avoid layout_copy, (C) adjust batching heuristic to prefer larger batches when kv-cache prefix distribution heavy.

maria (runtime): I prototyped (B) locally: adding 0-padding to head dim allocation removed the memcpy and matched v3 kernel, reducing tail back to baseline in my run. Need to validate memory/reg correctness.

zach (eng): nice. can you open a PR with the prototype and a perf test in the CI matrix? Tag me for review.

maria (runtime): will do. I'll also add an autotune job sweep for arch=A100/H100 with head_dims=[24,30,48,64] across seqlen=[256,512,1024,2048] and include causal flag.

perf-ci-bot: Created perf job: jobs/1865432100-autotune-sdpa-tiling. Results will post to #eng-runtime when done.

arjun (ml-opt): long-term we should teach kernel selector to be sequence-length-aware (not just per-call, but distribution-aware) and to simulate KV-cache effective seqlen for a route. That's how we avoid oscillations when traffic mixes short+long.

jen (sre): timeline? if prototype is low-risk we can gate it behind a canary rollout on a subset of hosts.

maria (runtime): aiming for PR by EOD tomorrow, canary next week. I'll include a small invariant test that asserts no extra device memcpy for v3 path.

zach (eng): thanks for the triage. @arjun please coordinate autotune metric additions. :thumbsup:

maria (runtime): thanks — will follow up with links to PR and perf job results in this thread.
